name: finalize_mission_state
description: REQUIRED final-step tool. Submit all mission findings as a verified JSON state payload AND select Apple-inspired design tokens that match the mission's character. Call exactly once.

summary.description: A brief plain-text summary of all mission findings.

structured_data_payload.description: MANDATORY JSON object containing all mission findings. Use descriptive keys. Focus on completeness and accuracy.

design_tokens.description: REQUIRED visual theme. You are the Visual Director. Choose low-saturation, high-luminosity Apple-inspired palettes. Avoid neon or high-contrast hacker colors. Prefer muted, sophisticated tones.

primary_accent.description: Soft hex color for glows. Examples by context — Financial: '#5eead4' (soft teal). Travel: '#fbbf24' (warm amber). Research/Science: '#6ee7b7' (soft emerald). Creative: '#c084fc' (muted violet). General: '#8b9cf4' (soft indigo). Minimalist: '#94a3b8' (slate).

glass_intensity.description: Frosted-glass depth 0.0–1.0. Financial/dense data: 0.75. Travel/narrative: 0.55. Minimalist: 0.40. Research: 0.60.

layout_density.description: 'compact' for data-dense missions (tables, comparisons). 'spacious' for narrative, travel, creative.

border_radius.description: Card corner radius in px. Default 24. Use 16 for compact/fintech, 28–32 for organic/creative.

surface_opacity.description: Card background opacity 0.0–0.15. Keep low (0.05–0.08) for elegant frosted look. Higher values make cards more opaque.

layout_strategy.description: Frontend layout strategy. 'FocusOnCharts': mission has time-series or comparative data arrays → render charts. 'DataHeavy': many tables and metrics, use compact layout. 'Narrative': story-driven, spacious cards. 'Overview': balanced default.

verification_logs.description: Optional quality notes, data sources, or caveats.

suggested_widgets.description: Optional hints for specific frontend components. Format: 'ComponentType:payload_key'. E.g. ['ChartCard:price_history', 'ImageCard:product_visual']. Use ChartCard for time-series or comparative arrays. Use ImageCard when a visual anchor (scene description, product render) would enhance the data.
